newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hutchison Port welcomes Philippine court decision.
newsitem.headline: Hutchison Port welcomes Philippine court decision.

text.p: Hutchison Port Holdings, a wholly-owned unit of Hutchison Whampoa Ltd, said on Thursday it was pleased with a Philippine court decision to dismiss graft charges against four Subic Bay officials.
The four Subic Bay Metropolitan Authority (SBMA) executives awarded the tender to develop and operate the Subic Bay Container Terminal to Hutchison Port last August.
Hutchison Port said it was very pleased with the decision made by the Office of the Ombudsman, a special anti-corruption court, to dismiss the charges.
"We believe our position has been vindicated, and this will help boost our business development efforts to invest and operate ports in the region and elsewhere," Hutchison Port said in a statement.

Those cleared were chairman of the SBMA's prequalification bids and awards committee Ferdinand Aristorenas; committee members Ferdinand Hernandez and Armin Raquel-Santos; and head of the technical evaluation committee Michael Kho, the London-based Lloyd's List newspaper reported on Tuesday.

The investigation began after local port operator International Container Terminal Services Inc (ICTS) raised allegations that members of the SBMA appeared to have manipulated the bidding in favour of Hutchison Port, it said.
ICTS's bid for the contract was rejected on the grounds it would violate a Philippine law forbidding monopolies in the port industry, the paper said.
ICTS operates the Manila International Container Terminals.

In January, Philippine President Fidel Ramos told the SBMA to restart the bidding from scratch for the 25-year contract at the container terminal in the booming Subic Bay economic zone that has replaced a former U.S. military base.
Following the court ruling, SBMA chairman Richard Gordon urged Ramos to award the contract to Hutchison Port, Lloyd's List said.
"I personally feel a rebidding should no longer take place and Hutchison Port should be awarded the contract," it quoted Gordon as saying.
Hutchison Port told Reuters it would continue to monitor new developments in the project.
"We are still observing the developments and considering all possible options," a spokesman said.
